# Add Investor staff members

## Problem statement

The staff family has no member that manipulates the **market row** itself: every ability so far buffs income, reputation, costs, incidents or hand capacity. The Investor introduces a market-shaping role — one **free market re-roll per turn** that is **biased toward the business type where the Investor is employed** — giving players a reason to invest coins in scouting favourable offers rather than accepting the first row they see. Moving the Investor to a different business costs an action point, so the ability is a deliberate positioning decision rather than a free upgrade.

## Users

- **Main Street player (build planner)** — wants a market-manipulation tool that rewards placing an Investor next to the business type they are trying to grow.
- **Main Street player (mid-game)** — wants a coin-free way to dig for a missing synergy piece (e.g. a Food business while running a Food cluster).

Example user stories:

- As a Main Street player, I want a free market re-roll each turn while an Investor is employed, so that I can look for a better offer without paying the escalating re-roll cost (MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ).
- As a Main Street player, I want the Investor's free re-roll to be 75% likely to surface cards relevant to the business it is employed at, so that placing it near my cluster meaningfully improves my odds.
- As a Main Street player, I want to move the Investor to a different business for one action point, so that I can retarget the bias at a cost.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Investor card exists in the catalog.** A new `staff-investor` row is added to `src/card-data.csv` (feature flag `freeMarketRerollPerTurn`, bias `0.75`, no hand slots, generalist `allowedBusinessTypes`), with a tier assignment, cost, ongoing cost and description consistent with the staff ladder and the ×100 coin scale; it flows into the general market via the existing tier-gated staff deck (`createStaffDeck`).
- **AC2 — One free re-roll per turn.** While at least one Investor is employed, the player may perform **one** coin-free, action-free market re-roll per week/turn (no coin deduction, no action spent); multiple Investors do not stack (still one per turn). The free re-roll is gated by a per-turn flag reset at `WeekStart` alongside `peekUsedThisTurn`/`favourUsedThisTurn`, and it **advances the per-turn escalation counter** (`marketRefreshesThisTurn`, `MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ`) so the next paid re-roll costs the escalated price. Once used, further re-rolls fall back to the normal paid path.
- **AC3 — Relevance bias.** On the Investor's free re-roll, each drawn slot has a **75% chance** to be drawn from the "relevant" pool for the business the Investor is employed at, falling back to the fully random pool when the relevant pool is exhausted; the remaining probability is entirely random. Relevance is defined as a shared synergy type (business/community-space `synergyTypes`; event `targetSynergy`/effect; staff `allowedBusinessTypes` overlap with the hosting business's synergy types) — the free `refillSingleRowMarket` path is parameterised so the normal `refreshMarket`/`cycleMarketCards` paths stay fully random.
- **AC4 — All staff relocation costs an action point.** Relocating a hired staff member from one business to another is exposed as a player action and consumes **1 action point** for **all** staff (the existing `placeStaffOnBusiness` placement is action-free today and must be action-gated when used as a relocation; the initial placement at hire time remains part of the hire action). The move respects `allowedBusinessTypes` and employment-slot capacity, is undoable, and is persisted.
- **AC5 — UI & tooltips.** The market re-roll button/tooltip and the Investor's staff tooltip/employed-staff summary surface (a) whether the free re-roll is still available this turn and (b) the 75% relevance bias; the button label/tooltip reflect the coin-free state when available and the escalated cost when not. Wording stays consistent with the `MS-0MTIS895Y008XGQ1` "Research" rename if that lands first.
- **AC6 — Undo, save/load and determinism.** The per-turn free-re-roll flag, the per-turn escalation counter it increments (`marketRefreshesThisTurn`), the Investor's location and any bias state participate in undo/redo (`snapshotAction`) and in `MainStreetStateSerialize` (serialize + migrate backfill + deserialize), so mid-turn reload preserves both availability and the escalated next price; the bias draw uses the seeded RNG (`state.rng`) so same-seed ⇒ same-game determinism holds.
- **AC7 — Tests.** Unit/integration tests cover: catalog + CSV contract; free re-roll is coin-free, once per turn, resets at `WeekStart` and advances the escalation counter; the 75% relevance bias (deterministic with a seeded RNG) and its random fallback; movement action cost + undo + save/load round-trip; and existing re-roll/discount/action-economy tests are updated for the new card and counts.
- **AC8 — Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `README.md`, the Main Street rules docs (`core-rules-and-mechanics.md`, `content-design-and-progression.md`, `card-catalog.md`) and any relevant wiki or docs-site entries.
- **AC9 — Quality gate.** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **New mechanic, not just data.** The relevance bias and the free re-roll are new engine behaviour; they must be additive and must not change existing behaviour when no Investor is employed.
- **Single source of truth for re-roll cost.** The free re-roll must not silently bypass `refreshMarketCost()`; the paid path and its escalation (`MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ`) remain authoritative for non-free re-rolls, and the free re-roll must increment the same per-turn escalation counter.
- **Reuse the market composition model.** `refillSingleRowMarket` (`src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts`) enforces the ≥1-business row composition; the biased draw must preserve that invariant.
- **Placement/employment invariant.** `business.employedStaff` and `staff.employedAtSlot` are kept in sync by the existing placement helpers; the move action must route through them.
- **Art drift guard.** `tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts` requires every unique card name to map to dedicated art or a documented pending-art target, and forbids growing the art-less baseline (currently 79). The Investor therefore needs a dedicated 1024×1024 sprite **or** an explicit, producer-approved pending-art entry (see `MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E`).
- **Coin scale.** All coin values are ×100 (per the integer-economy migration); the Investor's cost/ongoing cost must follow the existing staff ladder (`MS-0MULWBSF9000Z64Z`).

## Existing state

- **No Investor exists** anywhere in the repo or worklog (searched `investor`, case-insensitive, excluding `node_modules`/`dist`); only the unrelated `Investor Bonanza` event fixture appears in a test.
- **Market re-roll is already action-free** (`core-rules-and-mechanics.md` §6.0 "Free operations: Market re-roll/refresh"), so "without using an action" means the Investor's re-roll is free of **coins** as well; the normal re-roll costs `REFRESH_MARKET_COST` (500, escalating per `MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ`).
- `refillSingleRowMarket(state)` (`src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts:162`) builds the row: 3 slots, ≥1 business, at most 1 upgrade / 1 event / 1 staff, drawing via `state.rng` (seeded).
- `refreshMarket(state)` / `refreshMarketCost(state)` / `canRefreshMarket(state)` live in `src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts`; discounts come from `refreshCostDiscount` staff and the Negotiator skill.
- **Staff placement is free today**: `placeStaffOnBusiness` (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts:880`) explicitly consumes no action/coins; `placeStaffOnBusinessCommand`/`removeStaffFromBusinessCommand` (`src/MainStreetCommands.ts:674/692`) wrap it in `snapshotAction`. There is currently **no** player-facing "move staff" action.
- Staff card fields live in `StaffCard` (`src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts:330`), parsed in `MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts` (CSV columns incl. `actionsPerTurn`, `peekOncePerTurn`, `allowedBusinessTypes`); the catalog currently holds **25** staff rows.
- Per-turn gates (`peekUsedThisTurn`, `favourUsedThisTurn`, `businessPlacedThisTurn`) are reset in `executeWeekStart` (`src/MainStreetEngineWeekStart.ts`).
- Card-count baselines that will shift when a staff row is added: `tests/main-street/group-f-staff-abilities-expansion.test.ts` (`toHaveLength(25)`), `tests/main-street/meta-progression.test.ts` (166 / 174 totals), `docs/main-street/card-catalog-baseline.json`, `docs/main-street/expanded-card-manifest.json`.

## Desired change

- **CSV/catalog:** add `staff-investor` with a new bias column (e.g. `marketRelevanceBias = 0.75`) plus a free-re-roll marker (e.g. `freeMarketRerollPerTurn`), no `handSlotsAdded`, generalist `allowedBusinessTypes`, and a description in the existing "reduces X by Y" house style.
- **Types/parsing:** add the new optional `StaffCard` fields and parse them in `MainStreetCardsTemplates` (numeric column for the bias; boolean/flag column for the ability).
- **Engine:** add `investorFreeRerollUsedThisTurn` state (reset at `WeekStart`), a `canUseFreeMarketReroll`/`useFreeMarketReroll` pair (coin-free, action-free, once per turn) that **increments `marketRefreshesThisTurn`**, and a `refillSingleRowMarket`-compatible biased draw parameterised by the hosting business's synergy types + `0.75`.
- **Movement:** add a move-staff engine function + command that charges 1 action via the existing weekly action budget for **any** staff relocation, reusing `placeStaffOnBusiness` semantics (adding the action gate at the command layer).
- **Serialization:** add the new state field to serialize, migrate (backfill `false`/`0`) and deserialize.
- **UI:** market re-roll button/tooltip shows the free re-roll availability; staff tooltip/employed-staff summary states the free re-roll + 75% bias; a move-staff affordance that costs an action.
- **Docs & art:** update the rules/catalog/progression docs; add the Investor sprite (or a documented pending-art entry) and regenerate `card-art-map.json`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/card-data.csv` — new `staff-investor` row (new bias column + free-re-roll flag; tier, cost, ongoing cost, description).
- `src/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` — `StaffCard.freeMarketRerollPerTurn?` / `StaffCard.marketRelevanceBias?` (+ doc comments).
- `src/MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts` — parse the new CSV columns into the new fields.
- `src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts` — free re-roll path (`canUseFreeMarketReroll` / `useFreeMarketReroll`), bias-aware `refreshMarket` variant, and cost/label reporting.
- `src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts` — parameterise `refillSingleRowMarket` with an optional relevance pool; keep the default path unchanged.
- `src/MainStreetEngineWeekStart.ts` — reset the per-turn free-re-roll flag.
- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — new per-turn state field (and serialized-state entry).
- `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` — serialize, migrate backfill (and deserialize) the new field.
- `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts` / `src/MainStreetCommands.ts` — move-staff engine function + command (1 action), free-re-roll command.
- `src/MainStreetStaffBuffs.ts` / `src/MainStreetStaffSkills.ts` — helpers to detect the employed Investor and its hosting business synergy types.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererMarket.ts`, `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerMarketActions.ts`, `src/scenes/MainStreetHudTooltips.ts` — free-re-roll button state, tooltip and availability text.
- `src/MainStreetFormatting.ts` — employed-staff summary / staff tooltip line for the new ability.
- `src/card-art-map.json`, `src/sprites/`, `src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` — Investor art (or a documented pending-art entry).
- `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — free re-roll, relevance bias, movement cost.
- `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md` — staff table row + ability cell.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog.md` — staff catalogue row.
- `docs/main-street/card-catalog-baseline.json`, `docs/main-street/expanded-card-manifest.json` — catalog baselines.
- `tests/main-street/` — new `investor-staff.test.ts` (free re-roll, bias, movement) plus updates to `refresh-market.test.ts`, `group-f-staff-abilities-expansion.test.ts`, `meta-progression.test.ts`, `staff-business-type-matching.test.ts`, `card-art.test.ts`, `hud-tooltips.test.ts`, `action-economy.test.ts` and any staff-count assertions.

## Related work

See **Related work (automated report)** below, plus manually identified items:

- `MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ` — "Reroll to cost more" (open): escalates the paid re-roll cost; its appendix explicitly leaves "free re-rolls do not advance the escalation counter" as an assumption to settle with this item.
- `MS-0MTIS895Y008XGQ1` — "Rename the reroll button 'Research'" (in-progress): touches the same market re-roll button/tooltip; coordinate wording and the free-re-roll affordance.
- `MS-0MTQ7S5EJ008MWD0` — "Some staff cards should add action points" (completed): establishes the weekly action budget and the staff card UI/action patterns the movement cost builds on.
- `MS-0MUMCVH3N007KT1M` — "Implement IT Specialist and Delivery Driver cost-reduction effects" (completed): most recent end-to-end staff-ability implementation (CSV → engine → docs → tests); follow its structure.
- `MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E` — "Assign dedicated card art to every Main Street card" (open): owns the art-less baseline; the Investor raises the drift-guard question.
- `MS-0MUAYBAHW007RMSL` — "Add a charity shop" (completed): precedent for adding a card and updating the catalog/count baselines.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Decision (free = coins-free, escalation-advancing):** because market re-roll is already action-free, "free re-roll, without using an action" means **no coin cost and no action cost**, but the free re-roll **advances** the per-turn escalation counter. *Confirmed by producer 2026-09-30.*
- **Decision (bias definition):** "relevant to the type of business they are currently located at" = shares a synergy type with the hosting business; businesses/community-space by `synergyTypes`, events by `targetSynergy`, staff by `allowedBusinessTypes` overlap. *Confirmed by producer 2026-09-30.*
- **Decision (bias application):** the 75% applies per drawn slot with a random fallback; the entire row is not a single 75% roll. *Confirmed by producer 2026-09-30.*
- **Decision (no stacking):** multiple Investors still grant a single free re-roll per turn (avoids a degenerate multi-Investor loop). *Confirmed by producer 2026-09-30.*
- **Decision (movement scope):** **all** staff relocation costs an action; the initial placement at hire time is unchanged. *Confirmed by producer 2026-09-30.*
- **Risk (scope creep / existing behaviour):** the re-roll cost item and the rename item touch the same button; implementing the free re-roll without advancing the counter would desynchronise the displayed price, and newly action-gating **all** staff relocation changes an existing free operation (and its tests). Mitigation: keep `refreshMarketCost()` authoritative, increment the shared counter on the free re-roll, and update the staff-placement tests in the same change.
- **Risk (determinism/tests):** adding a card changes seeded deck draws and several fixed-count baselines; many fixtures inline counts. Mitigation: update the documented baselines and count assertions in the same change, and cover the bias with a seeded-RNG test.
- **Risk (art drift guard):** a new art-less card fails `card-art.test.ts`; either supply a sprite or get a producer-approved pending-art entry, otherwise the item is blocked by `MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E`.
- **Risk (save compat):** forgetting the migrate backfill leaves old saves with `undefined` and a throwing/NaN free-re-roll gate. Mitigation: backfill in `migrateSerializedState` and assert a round-trip.
- **Risk (balance):** a free re-roll per turn plus a 75% biased row is a strong information advantage; cost/tier may need balancing (`balancing-methodology.md`). Mitigation: pick a mid/premium tier and revisit after playtest.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

**Round 1 (route: herdr auto-dispatch, 2026-09-30; answered by the producer 2026-09-30).**

- **Q1 (free re-roll semantics):** "The market re-roll is already action-free, so what does the Investor's 'free re-roll' free you from, and does it stack/interact with the escalating cost (`MS-0MTR6ZRF5007PWNZ`)? Options: (a) one **coin-free** re-roll per turn, does **not** advance the escalation counter, multiple Investors do **not** stack; (b) one coin-free re-roll per Investor (stacks); (c) the free re-roll also resets the escalation counter; (d) freeform."
  **Answer (producer, 2026-09-30):** one coin-free, action-free re-roll per turn; it **does advance the escalation counter**; multiple Investors do **not** stack.

- **Q2 (relevance definition & application):** "How is 'relevant to the type of business they are currently located at' defined, and how does the 75% apply? Options: (a) a shared synergy type (business/community-space `synergyTypes`, event `targetSynergy`, staff `allowedBusinessTypes` overlap), applied **per drawn slot** with random fallback; (b) relevant by exact business name only; (c) the **whole row** is 75% likely to be relevant; (d) freeform."
  **Answer (producer, 2026-09-30):** as recommended — **(a)** shared synergy type, applied per drawn slot, with random fallback.

- **Q3 (movement cost & scope):** "Staff placement is action-free today. Should the Investor's move cost an action point, and does that apply to all staff? Options: (a) **Investor only** pays 1 action to relocate; other staff stay free; (b) **all staff** relocation costs 1 action; (c) the move is free but limited to once per turn; (d) freeform."
  **Answer (producer, 2026-09-30):** **(b)** — **all** staff relocation costs 1 action.

**Secondary assumptions (not asked in Round 1, to keep to the ≤3-question limit):**

- **Card economics (default):** `staff-investor` is a generalist (all synergy types), `handSlotsAdded: 0`, tier 5, cost 1000, ongoing 125 — mirroring the tier-5 specialist band (Financial Advisor). *Recorded as an assumption; the producer may re-balance.*
- **Art (default):** add a dedicated 1024×1024 Investor sprite and regenerate `card-art-map.json`; if art cannot be produced, request a producer-approved pending-art entry so the drift guard passes.
- **Rename coordination (default):** implement the free-re-roll affordance on the existing re-roll button so it survives the `MS-0MTIS895Y008XGQ1` "Research" rename without conflicting wording.

**Research finding (agent, 2026-09-30):** The free re-roll and relevance bias are **not** implemented anywhere (repo + worklog search). The re-roll is already action-free and coin-costed (`src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts`); `refillSingleRowMarket` (`src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts:162`) is the single composition point; staff placement is action-free (`src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts:880`). This item is therefore a **new mechanic + card + docs + art** change, not a data-only change.

## Goal (user story)

As a player who just reached the win threshold in endless mode, I want an "Enter Endless Mode" button on the end-game dialog so I can continue playing beyond the threshold.

## Context

CG-0MTIILU5V006GCN4 wired the endless-mode logic: when `config.endlessMode === true` and a player reaches the score threshold, the engine sets `endReason = 'score_threshold_continue'` and keeps `gameResult = 'playing'`. The end-game dialog (`MainStreetOverlayContent.showGameOverOverlay`) already reads `endReason` for display, but the player has no way to actually continue — the only options are "Play Again" (restart) and "Menu" (quit). This leaves the endless-mode feature inert from a player-facing perspective.

## Scope

- Add an "Enter Endless Mode" button to the end-game dialog when `endReason === 'score_threshold_continue'`.
- When pressed, the button dismisses the overlay and resumes gameplay from the current state (no restart).
- The button is hidden in all other end-reasons (normal win, bankruptcy, turn exhaustion, etc.).

## Out of scope

- Competitive mode endless mode (separate CG-0MT5X3GMA007EG30 children).
- UI changes to the main menu or difficulty selector.
- Any Monte Carlo or AI changes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **AC1:** End-game dialog shows an "Enter Endless Mode" button when `state.endReason === 'score_threshold_continue'`.
- [ ] **AC2:** Pressing the button dismisses the game-over overlay, resets `endReason` to `null` (or appropriate continuation value), and resumes the game loop — the game continues playing and scoring.
- [ ] **AC3:** The button is not shown when `endReason` is anything other than `score_threshold_continue`.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — `showGameOverOverlay()` adds the button.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — Resume logic after button press (dismiss overlay, call engine continuation).

# Reroll to cost more

## Problem Statement

Main Street's market re-roll currently costs a flat 500 coins (`REFRESH_MARKET_COST`), so a player can re-roll repeatedly within the same turn at the same price and brute-force a favourable market row. The cost should escalate with every re-roll made in the same turn (500, 750, 1000, and +250 each time) and reset at the start of each turn.

## Users

- **Main Street player** — "As a player, I want each successive market re-roll in a turn to cost 250 more than the last, so that re-rolling is a meaningful, escalating economic decision rather than a cheap reset of the market row."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **AC1 — Escalating cost:** Within a single turn, the first re-roll costs 500 coins, the second 750, the third 1000, and each subsequent re-roll costs 250 more than the previous one.
2. **AC2 — Turn reset:** The re-roll escalation resets to the 500 base at the start of each turn (the `WeekStart` day boundary, alongside the other per-turn gates).
3. **AC3 — Staff discounts preserved:** Existing refresh-cost discounts (Accountant `refreshCostDiscount`, Negotiator specialization skill) continue to be subtracted from the escalated base cost, clamped at 0 (never negative).
4. **AC4 — Legality & UI:** `canRefreshMarket()` and the re-roll button label/tooltip report the current escalated cost, and the button is disabled (with the existing "not enough coins" reason) when the player cannot afford it.
5. **AC5 — Undo & persistence:** The per-turn re-roll count participates in undo (a re-roll can be reversed) and in save/load serialization, so reloading mid-turn preserves the escalated price.
6. **AC6 — Tests:** Unit tests cover the 500/750/1000 progression, the per-turn reset, discount interaction, and undo/save-load round-trip; affected existing tests are updated.
7. **AC7 — Documentation:** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
8. **AC8 — Quality gate:** Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Only the escalation schedule is new; staff discount values are unchanged.
- The refresh cost must stay centralised in `refreshMarketCost()` so every call site (legality check, command, UI) sees the same escalated price.
- Free-reroll abilities are not yet implemented (see CG-0MTISBYLS009936W); they are out of scope for this item.

## Existing State

- `REFRESH_MARKET_COST = 500` in `src/MainStreetCardsConstants.ts` (re-exported via `MainStreetCards.ts`).
- `refreshMarketCost(state)` in `src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts` subtracts summed staff `refreshCostDiscount` plus the Negotiator skill discount and clamps at 0.
- `canRefreshMarket(state)` gates on `MarketPhase` and affordability; `refreshMarket(state)` deducts the cost, discards visible cards, refills the row, and logs.
- `refreshMarketCommand(state)` in `src/MainStreetCommands.ts` wraps the action in `snapshotAction` for undo/redo.
- There is currently **no** per-turn re-roll counter on `MainStreetState`.
- `executeWeekStart()` in `src/MainStreetEngineWeekStart.ts` already resets the other per-turn gates (`peekUsedThisTurn`, `favourUsedThisTurn`, `businessPlacedThisTurn`).
- The re-roll UI label already renders `refreshMarketCost(s.state)` in `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererMarket.ts`.
- `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` lists fields explicitly in three places (serialize, migrate backfill, deserialize), so a new counter must be added to all three.
- `tests/main-street/refresh-market.test.ts` (AC2) currently asserts "unlimited per turn while affordable" at a flat cost — this assertion must change.

## Desired Change

- Add a `REFRESH_MARKET_COST_STEP` (working name) constant = 250 next to `REFRESH_MARKET_COST`.
- Add a `marketRefreshesThisTurn: number` field to `MainStreetState` (default 0), documented in `MainStreetStateTypes.ts`.
- `refreshMarketCost(state)` returns `Math.max(0, REFRESH_MARKET_COST + REFRESH_MARKET_COST_STEP * marketRefreshesThisTurn - discounts)`.
- `refreshMarket(state)` increments `marketRefreshesThisTurn` on a successful re-roll (so the reported/charged cost is the pre-increment value).
- `executeWeekStart()` resets `marketRefreshesThisTurn = 0`.
- Initialise the counter in `setupMainStreetGame`; serialise it, backfill it in `migrateSerializedState`, and restore it in the deserializer.
- Update the affected tests and the Main Street rules documentation.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetCardsConstants.ts` — add the 250 escalation step constant alongside `REFRESH_MARKET_COST`.
- `src/MainStreetCards.ts` — re-export the new constant if it follows the existing barrel pattern.
- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — add the `marketRefreshesThisTurn` state field (and serialized-state type entry).
- `src/MainStreetMarketRefill.ts` — `refreshMarketCost()` computes the escalated base; `refreshMarket()` increments the counter.
- `src/MainStreetEngineWeekStart.ts` — reset the counter at `WeekStart`.
- `src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts` — initialise the counter to 0.
- `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` — serialize, migrate (backfill 0), and deserialize the counter.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererMarket.ts` — verify the label/tooltip/disabled state use the escalated `refreshMarketCost()` (likely no code change; confirm).
- `tests/main-street/refresh-market.test.ts` — replace the flat "unlimited per turn" case with escalation + reset coverage.
- `tests/main-street/staff-skill-buff-wiring.test.ts`, `tests/main-street/group-f-staff-abilities-expansion.test.ts` — update discount assertions for the escalated/unchanged first-roll cost.
- `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — document the escalating re-roll cost and per-turn reset.

## Risks and Assumptions

- **Assumption (discounts):** staff discounts keep applying to the escalated base, clamped at 0 — pending producer confirmation (see Appendix).
- **Assumption (free re-rolls):** a free re-roll does not advance the escalation counter — pending producer confirmation (see Appendix).
- **Assumption (unbounded):** escalation has a fixed 250 step and no upper bound; affordability is the practical cap — pending producer confirmation (see Appendix).
- **Risk (undo/redo):** if the counter is not part of the undo snapshot, undoing a re-roll would refund coins while leaving the higher next price, producing an inconsistent cost. Mitigation: rely on the existing whole-state snapshot and assert undo restores both coins and counter.
- **Risk (save/load):** forgetting the migrate backfill would make pre-existing saves load `undefined` and NaN the cost. Mitigation: backfill `?? 0` in `migrateSerializedState`.
- **Risk (existing tests):** the "unlimited per turn" assertion and flat-cost discount assertions will fail once escalation lands. Mitigation: update them in the same change.

# Problem statement

The contextual first-bank hint overlay (CG-0MT3JK16W006A66P) fires during the tutorial when the player ends a turn with spare actions, creating a "dead end" that interrupts tutorial progression and confuses the tutorial state machine. The hint is designed for normal gameplay and should not fire while the tutorial is active.

## Users

- **New players** completing the Main Street tutorial — they expect a linear, guided experience. An unexpected banking hint overlay mid-tutorial interrupts this flow, potentially showing a stale or completed tutorial step after the hint is dismissed.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Banking hint does not fire during tutorial:** The contextual first-bank hint trigger in `MainStreetTurnController.endTurn()` must check that `tutorialController.isActive` is `false` (i.e., the tutorial is not active). The hint must never fire while the tutorial overlay is showing or a tutorial step is pending.
2. **Banking hint fires in normal gameplay:** The hint continues to fire exactly once when a non-tutorial player ends a turn with `actionsRemaining > 0`, respecting the persistence flag (`hasSeenBankingHint`).
3. **No regression to tutorial flow:** Existing tutorial steps, overlay lifecycle, and step progression remain unchanged. The tutorial still completes through all 26 steps without interruption from the banking hint.
4. **No regression to banking hint:** The hint still triggers correctly in normal gameplay after the tutorial is complete (on the first end-turn with spare actions).
5. **All tests pass:** Existing tutorial unit and browser tests pass; no new failures introduced.

## Constraints

- **Minimal change:** Only the trigger condition in `MainStreetTurnController.endTurn()` needs modification (one logical operator change). No new fields, no structural changes.
- **Tutorial-layer only:** The fix is entirely within Main Street's tutorial wiring; no core-engine, card-system, or UI component changes.
- **Existing banking hint implementation preserved:** The `BANKING_HINT_STEP`, `renderBankingHint()`, and `TutorialState` banking hint flag remain unchanged.

## Existing state

- **CG-0MT3JK16W006A66P** implemented the contextual first-bank hint with the following trigger in `MainStreetTurnController.endTurn()`:
  ```ts
  if (tut?.isActive && s.state.actionsRemaining > 0) {
      pendingBankingHint = true;
      // persist flag via TutorialState
  }
  ```
- This condition fires when the tutorial is **active** AND the player has spare actions.
- The `renderBankingHint()` method saves the current tutorial step, shows the banking hint overlay, and on dismiss tries to restore the saved step — but if the tutorial step has already advanced (e.g., T6 End Turn completed), the restoration shows a stale step, creating the "dead end."
- The intent from the original brief (CG-0MT3JK16W006A66P) was that the hint fires **once per save** on the first bankable end-turn — but the implementation does not distinguish between tutorial and normal gameplay contexts.

## Desired change

Change the trigger condition in `MainStreetTurnController.endTurn()` from:
```ts
if (tut?.isActive && s.state.actionsRemaining > 0)
```
to:
```ts
if (!tut?.isActive && s.state.actionsRemaining > 0)
```

This ensures the banking hint only fires in normal gameplay (after the tutorial is complete), never during the tutorial.

## Key Files

- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts` — One-line fix: invert the `tut?.isActive` check in the banking hint trigger (endTurn path, ~line 221).

## Related work

- **CG-0MT3JK16W006A66P** (completed, merged) — Main Street: tutorial coverage for action banking (parent feature that introduced the contextual first-bank hint).
- **CG-0MT3IOPZB005LNAR** (completed, merged) — Main Street: action banking (engine-level banking logic).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** If the producer believes the banking hint should also fire during the tutorial (e.g., as an optional teaching moment), that would require a different design — but the title and description indicate this is clearly unintended.
- **No edge cases:** The banking hint has a one-shot persistence flag; if the hint never fires during the tutorial (which is the fix), it will fire on the player's first non-tutorial end-turn with spare actions — this is the intended behaviour.

Main Street has no charity shop: a low-cost, Culture-synergy business that trades a modest income for a steady reputation trickle. - **As a player**, I can buy a Charity Shop for 300 coins and place it on the street, where it produces a small income and a steady reputation gain each turn, giving me an early Culture-synergy building with a reputation focus.

1. **Card data.** `src/card-data.csv` contains a new business row with exactly: `family = business`, `id = biz-charity-shop`, `name = Charity Shop`, `cost = 300`, `baseIncome = 150`, `synergyTypes = Culture`, `upgradePath` empty (standalone), `maxLevel = 0`, `reputationPerTurn = 15`, `ongoingCost = 75`, `tier = 2`, plus a non-empty `description` and `art_notes`. # Write storylines — harden, document, and extend the Main Street storyline system

**Epic.** Producer decisions (2026-09-26): **Q1 = epic**; **Q2 = implement all
improvements now**; **Q3 = keep Main Street-specific, but design with an eye to
extracting into core-engine in future — cutting corners is acceptable now, but
do not make extraction impossible.**

## Problem statement

Main Street has a *rough* storyline implementation: incident event cards can
carry a dual choice (`hasChoices` / `acceptNextCardId` / `rejectNextCardId`)
and the player's Accept/Reject decision schedules the next card in a chain
(`CG-0MTSHG8RP008E128`). The mechanic works and is tested, but it is thin,
implicit, and undocumented:

- the branching model supports only binary choices with one successor per
  branch, with no storyline identity/grouping;
- there is no static validation — a dangling chain link is only logged at
  runtime (`Chain card X not found in card data.`);
- there is no authoring, validation, or visualisation tooling (chains are
  hand-edited inside a 155-row CSV);
- no documentation explains how storylines are created and managed; and
- storylines are invisible to players as stories — they see two opaque
  buttons and no memory of how their choices shaped events.

This makes storylines hard to extend safely and invisible as a source of
player agency.

## Users

- **Content designers / producers** — author, extend and balance storylines
  (new chains, retro-fitting existing incidents) without editing engine code,
  and see the shape of a storyline at a glance.
- **TCE / Main Street developers** — need a documented, validated, and
  flexible data model with clear seams so storyline changes cannot silently
  break, and so the mechanic can later move to the core engine.
- **Players** — should feel their choices shape an unfolding story, with
  visible continuity (what they chose, what it led to, which thread is still
  running) rather than two opaque buttons.
- **AI / Monte Carlo** — need a decision policy that remains correct as the
  branching model and option counts grow.

### Example user stories

- "As a content designer, I want to define a storyline declaratively and run a
  validator, so I know every branch resolves before I ship it."
- "As a developer, I want a documented storyline model and an authoring guide,
  so I can add a multi-step chain without reverse-engineering the engine."
- "As a player, I want a storyline journal that shows my past choices and what
  they led to, so my decisions feel like they build a narrative."
- "As a player, I want to know which story threads are still running, so
  recurring events feel connected rather than random."
- "As a producer, I want a prioritised roadmap of further storyline
  improvements, so I can schedule the next iteration."

## Scope areas (all to be implemented — Q2 = all now)

### A. Model & engine hardening (+ future extraction seam)

1. **Storyline identity/grouping** — optional `storylineId` (+ display
   `storylineTitle`) on `EventCard` and in the CSV, grouping chain cards into
   named storylines. Backward compatible.
2. **Generalised option model** — support an ordered list of options (each
   with a label, a successor card id, and an effect policy of apply/skip),
   while preserving legacy `hasChoices` / `acceptNextCardId` /
   `rejectNextCardId` semantics byte-for-byte.
3. **Extraction seam** — isolate storyline definitions, state and resolution
   behind a small game-agnostic interface/registry and pure functions, with
   migration notes, so the mechanic can move to `src/core-engine` later
   without rewriting callers. Corners may be cut, but the boundary must exist
   and be documented.
4. **Static validation** — every link resolves; no dangling, duplicate or
   unknown references; sinks and cycles are intentional. Validation fails
   loudly (non-zero exit), not just via a runtime log.
5. **Invariants preserved** — undo/redo, save/load (old saves load), deferred
   end-of-turn mutation, transcript shape and AI resolution stay correct for
   all option counts.

### B. Documentation

6. Canonical **`docs/main-street/storylines.md`**: concepts, data model + CSV
   columns, resolution lifecycle, AI policy, tooling usage, an end-to-end
   authoring walkthrough with a worked example, an authoring checklist, and a
   documented extraction path to core-engine.
7. **`docs/DEVELOPER.md`** and **`example-games/main-street/README.md`**
   cross-reference the doc and list the new CSV columns and scripts.
8. A **doc-drift test** asserts the docs exist and that documented chain
   examples match the shipped CSV.
9. A prioritised **future-improvements roadmap** (tooling + player agency)
   documenting anything deliberately deferred, with deferred ideas captured as
   work items.

### C. Tooling (implemented)

10. **Validator** — `scripts/validate-storylines.ts` + an npm script
    (`validate:storylines`), wired into the test suite / pre-push so
    regressions fail the build.
11. **Graph / manifest export** — tool to emit a storyline graph or manifest
    (`--format mermaid|json`) plus a committed generated artefact and a JSON
    schema.
12. **Authoring helper** — a CLI (or equivalent documented commands) to add and
    link storyline cards safely, without hand-editing CSV internals.

### D. Player agency (implemented)

13. **Named storylines surfaced** in the choice dialog and activity log.
14. **Storyline journal/history overlay** — review past choices and outcomes,
    accessible from the HUD, using the standard overlay pattern and
    reduced-motion behaviour, backed by the existing transcript/log.
15. **Choice clarity** — explanatory tooltips/labels for each option that
    explain consequence semantics **without** revealing the escalation card
    (preserving the designed tension).
16. **Outcome feedback** — each resolved choice produces a concise narrative
    "story update" line tied to its `storylineId`.
17. **Continuity / foreshadowing** — an active/recurring-thread indicator while
    a storyline is in play (including cycles).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Storyline metadata** — `EventCard` (and the CSV) supports an optional
   `storylineId` and `storylineTitle`; the parser populates them; cards
   without them behave exactly as before. Covered by unit tests.
2. **Generalised option model** — the engine supports an arbitrary ordered
   list of options (label, successor card id, effect policy apply/skip);
   legacy `hasChoices`/`acceptNextCardId`/`rejectNextCardId` cards resolve
   identically. Covered by unit tests proving legacy-equivalence and a
   multi-option resolution.
3. **Extraction seam** — storyline definition/state/resolution are behind a
   documented game-agnostic interface/registry boundary with pure functions
   and explicit migration notes in the docs; no caller reaches into
   Main-Street-only internals for resolution.
4. **Static validation passes** — every `acceptNextCardId`/`rejectNextCardId`
   (and any new option link) in `card-data.csv` resolves to an existing card;
   no dangling/duplicate/unknown references; validation exits non-zero on
   failure and is enforced in the test suite or pre-push hook.
5. **Invariants preserved** — undo/redo, save/load (old saves without new
   fields load), deferred end-of-turn mutation, transcript `event-choice`
   records, and AI resolution remain correct for all option counts; covered by
   unit tests.

6. **Canonical documentation** — `docs/main-street/storylines.md` exists and
   documents concepts, the data model and CSV columns, the resolution
   lifecycle (deferred `pendingEventChoice`, option paths, deck insertion,
   undo/redo, save/load, transcript), the AI policy, tooling usage, a
   step-by-step authoring walkthrough with a worked example, an authoring
   checklist, and the core-engine extraction path.
7. **Cross-references updated** — `docs/DEVELOPER.md` and
   `example-games/main-street/README.md` reference the new doc and list the new
   CSV columns and scripts.
8. **Doc-drift guard** — at least one test/lint asserts the canonical doc
   exists and that its documented chain examples match the shipped CSV.
9. **Future-improvements roadmap** — the documentation contains a prioritised
   roadmap of further tooling and player-agency improvements, and any deferred
   ideas are captured as separate work items.

10. **Validator script** — `scripts/validate-storylines.ts` plus an npm script
    (`validate:storylines`), returning non-zero on invalid storylines and
    covered by tests against both valid and deliberately broken fixtures.
11. **Graph/manifest export** — a tool emits the storyline graph/manifest
    (`--format mermaid|json`); a generated artefact and JSON schema are
    committed, and a test asserts the emitted graph matches the CSV.
12. **Authoring helper** — a documented CLI (or equivalent) can add a
    storyline card/link safely and validate the result; the workflow is covered
    by the authoring guide and at least one test.

13. **Named storylines surfaced** — the choice dialog and activity log show the
    storyline name (e.g. "Tax Troubles — …") when available, with a
    reduced-motion-safe presentation.
14. **Journal/history overlay** — a player can open a storyline journal from
    the HUD that lists past choices and their outcomes; it uses
    `createOverlayBackground`/`createOverlayButton`, parents elements into
    `hudContainer`, and is covered by a browser test.
15. **Choice clarity** — option buttons carry tooltips/labels explaining
    consequence semantics without revealing the escalation card; covered by a
    test.
16. **Outcome feedback** — each resolved choice emits a concise narrative
    "story update" line tied to its storyline; covered by a unit test.
17. **Continuity indicator** — an active/recurring-storyline indicator is
    visible while a storyline is in play and cleared when it ends; covered by a
    test.

18. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including
    code comments, `README`, and any relevant `docs/` entries.
19. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Backward compatibility** — cards without storyline fields behave exactly
  as before; existing `hasChoices` cards are unchanged; old saves load with
  missing fields defaulted.
- **Determinism / replay safety** — storyline resolution and chain-card
  insertion must not consume RNG or wall-clock time; transcripts stay
  replayable and deterministic.
- **No cost model change** — event choices remain free (no daily-action cost).
- **Preserve designed tension** — choice clarity must not preview the
  escalation card; the "unknown consequence" tension is intentional.
- **Extraction seam, not extraction** — the mechanic stays Main Street-specific
  for now; corners may be cut but the boundaries must not make a later move to
  `src/core-engine` a rewrite.
- **Existing event-flow decisions preserved** — deferred end-of-turn mutation,
  undo/redo semantics, AI difficulty policy and tutorial exclusion of choice
  events must not regress.
- **No new runtime dependency** beyond the existing Node/Vitest/scripts
  toolchain for the tooling.

## Existing state (repo research)

### Data model
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` — `EventCard` has
  `hasChoices?: boolean`, `acceptNextCardId?: string | null`,
  `rejectNextCardId?: string | null` (`DurationEventCard` inherits them).
- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — header already contains the three
  columns. **7 choice cards** ship: `evt-tax` (→ `evt-tax-inquiry`), `evt-flu-outbreak`

- `MainStreetStateSerialize.ts` — serialises/backfills `pendingEventChoice`.
- `MainStreetCommands.ts` — snapshot-based undo/redo of the choice.
- `MainStreetTranscript.ts` — records `{ type: 'event-choice', eventId,
  cardName, option, acceptNextCardId, rejectNextCardId }`.

### UI
- `scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — `showEventChoiceDialog(event,
  onAccept, onReject)` (Accept/Reject buttons, no escalation preview, overlay
  depth conventions).
- `scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — shows the dialog when
  `choicePending` is observed; reduced-motion aware.

### AI
- `MainStreetEngineScoring.ts` — `decideEventChoice(state, event, difficulty)`
  (Easy: always accept; Medium: accept if manageable; Hard: static full-chain
  severity comparison + `AI_EVENT_CHOICE_SIGNIFICANTLY_WORSE_RATIO`).
- `MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — `resolveAiEventChoice()` resolves pending choices
  in headless/AI turns.

### Tests
- `tests/main-street/chain-content.test.ts`, `event-choice*.test.ts`,
  `MainStreetEventChoice*.test.ts`, `MainStreetAiEventChoice.test.ts`,
  `ai-choice.test.ts`, `tutorial-choice-exclusion.test.ts`,
  `event-choice-dialog*.browser.test.ts`, `incident-*.test.ts`.

### Gaps observed
- **No documentation** of the storyline model or authoring process in `docs/`
  (only a passing mention in `docs/main-street/content-design-and-progression.md`).
- **No static validation tooling** — dangling links only logged at runtime.
- **No authoring/visualisation tooling** — no schema, generator or graph view.
- **Binary-only branching** and **no storyline identity/history/journal**.
- **Content child still open** — `CG-0MTT7FC7A000AA58` ("Content: New chain
  cards and retro-fitting") is `status=open`, `stage=plan_complete`, despite
  the chain content appearing to ship; reconcile it.

## Desired change

1. **Harden** the model: add storyline identity, static validation, and fix
   code-comment/documentation gaps; reconcile the open content child.
2. **Generalise, with a seam**: support an ordered option list while preserving
   legacy accept/reject, behind a documented game-agnostic boundary that can
   later move to `src/core-engine`.
3. **Document** the full lifecycle end to end for content designers and
   developers.
4. **Implement** the tooling (validator, graph/manifest export, authoring
   helper) and player-agency improvements (named storylines, journal, clarity,
   feedback, continuity indicator).
5. **Test** the hardened model, tooling and player-facing behaviour, and guard
   against doc/code drift.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `docs/main-street/storylines.md` — **new** canonical documentation.
- `docs/DEVELOPER.md` — cross-reference / short summary section.
- `example-games/main-street/README.md` — CSV column reference + scripts.
- `example-games/main-street/card-data.csv` — storyline metadata + links.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardsTypes.ts` — model + extraction seam
  types.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardsTemplates.ts` — CSV parsing.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — resolution,
  `pushChainCard`, option-list support.
- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — `PendingEventChoice`
  shape.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts` — dialog,
  journal overlay, tooltips.
- `example-games/main-street/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — HUD
  wiring for the journal/continuity indicator.
- `scripts/validate-storylines.ts` — **new** validator.
- `scripts/storyline-graph.ts` (or similar) + `schemas/…storyline…json` —
  **new** export + schema.
- `tests/main-street/` — model, validator, tooling, player-agency and
  doc-drift tests.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope risk (epic)** — "implement all improvements now" is broad; the epic
  must be decomposed into independently reviewable children so a stalled slice
  does not block the rest. *Mitigation:* plan will break this into
  vertical slices.
- **Over-engineering risk** — the generalised option model could destabilise a
  shipped mechanic. *Mitigation:* legacy-equivalence tests; accept/reject
  remains a first-class compatibility path.
- **Extraction-seam drift** — the seam could decay into Main-Street-only
  internals. *Mitigation:* document the boundary and the migration path; keep
  resolution pure.
- **UI complexity** — a journal overlay plus tooltips plus a continuity
  indicator touch many HUD paths. *Mitigation:* reuse the established overlay
  pattern and depth convention; reduced-motion support.
- **Doc/code drift** — *Mitigation:* doc-drift test.
- **Content/engine coupling** — chain links live in a hand-edited CSV;
  validation must fail loudly. *Mitigation:* AC4/AC10.
- **Assumption** — "storylines" means the Main Street incident event-chain
  system; no other storyline implementation exists in the repo.

  designers; player-facing narrative prose remains content work.
- **Assumption** — CHANGELOG is managed by the release pipeline and is out of

# Ensure every Main Street card has dedicated card art (1024×1024 source)

## Problem statement

Every Main Street card renders a square art zone in its top-left corner, but
**108 of the 171 unique cards in `card-data.csv` currently render the same
generic `Fallback` sprite**, so the bulk of the deck is visually
indistinguishable. A player cannot tell an `Upgrade to Patisserie` from a
`Chef` from a `Rainy Day` at a glance, which undermines the 64×64 left-art
redesign's whole purpose.

## Users

- **Player (market / hand / street):** needs to recognise a card by its art
  without reading the title — especially when cards overlap in hand or stack
  on the street.
- **Content author:** needs a documented, testable rule for what art a card
  resolves to, so new cards cannot silently reintroduce `Fallback` art.
- **Engine maintainer:** needs one art-resolution path shared by the runtime
  generator and the static SVG exporter, guarded by a regression test.

User stories:

- As a player, when I look at the market, I can tell any two cards apart by
  their art alone.
- As an upgrade card, I show the art of the business I enhance under my new
  display name, so my purpose is obvious.
- As a content author, when I add a card to `card-data.csv`, the test suite
  tells me if I forgot to give it art.

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-26)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q1 | Art scope / strategy | **Option A — reuse-first.** Actively **duplicate the existing art under the new (card/display) name**, and produce **new art only where necessary** (no suitable existing art). |
| Q2 | Art production ownership | **The producer will produce the new sprites.** This item still owns the mapping, resolver, regeneration tooling and the drift guard. |
| Q3 | Event mapping granularity | **Map events by `trigger` × `targetSynergy` category** (a documented, generated mapping). |

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-29)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q4 | Source-art size | The producer provides **1024×1024** source art (`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`). The “64×64” is the on-card display zone, not the production size. |
| Q5 | Staff art granularity | **One sprite per staff role** (24 sprites). |
| Q6 | Event-category art | **Unique (bespoke) sprite per `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category** — representatives are not reused. |
| Q7 | Drift-guard tightening | **Yes** — tighten the guard to a strict “zero `Fallback` for every card in `card-data.csv`” assertion once the sprites land, in the same change. |
| Q8 | Duplicate-name clash | **Rename to remove the clashes**: business `Florist` → `Flower Shop`; event `Community Garden` → `Garden Party`. |

Art-production ownership (Q2, 2026-09-26) is unchanged: the producer supplies
all new source sprites.

## Existing state (verified 2026-09-26, `dev` @ 933644bc)

Resolution path (all four card families call it with the card's `name`):

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` → `resolveCardArtName()` /
  `hasDedicatedCardArt()`: (1) spelling alias → (2) exact name → (3)
  `Fallback`.
- Map built by `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs`
  from committed `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` files into
  `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json`.
- A second consumer, `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`,
  duplicates the alias/lookup logic and must be kept in step.

Verified counts:

- `card-data.csv`: **173 rows / 171 unique names** (duplicate names across
  families: `Florist` = business + staff, `Community Garden` = community-space
  + event → name-keyed resolution shares one sprite).
- Committed sprites: **62 dedicated + `Fallback`** (63 map entries).
- Cards resolving today: **65** (63 exact + 2 via aliases).
- **Cards rendering `Fallback`: 108**:

| Family              | Cards | Resolving | Missing |
|---------------------|------:|----------:|--------:|
| business            |    30 |        28 |       2 |
| community-space     |     8 |         1 |       7 |
| upgrade             |    39 |         0 |      39 |
| staff               |    25 |         1 |      24 |
| event               |    71 |        35 |      36 |
| **Total**           |  **173** | **65** | **108** |

Every missing card already has an `art_notes` description in `card-data.csv`
(the source the existing 1024×1024 sprites were built from). There is **no
in-repo image generator** — the existing sprites were committed out-of-band
(commit `05026750`), and the producer will continue producing new art the same
way.

## Size clarification (reviewed 2026-09-29)

The “64×64” in the original title is the **on-card display zone** — a layout
dimension in SVG user units — **not** the size of the source art to produce.
Code review of the generator and renderer confirms three distinct layers:

| Layer | Size | Where | Role |
|-------|-----:|-------|------|
| On-card art zone | 64×64 | `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` (`GRAPHIC_*`) | SVG layout box only |
| Embedded bitmap | 256×256 | `src/card-art-map.json` (`artResolution`) | WebP `data:` URI in the SVG |
| **Source art** | **1024×1024** | `src/sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` | Generator input |

`src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` only loads files named
`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` (`SOURCE_SUFFIX = '_1024_x_1024.png'`) and downscales
each to 256×256 WebP (`ART_RESOLUTION = 256`). Phaser rasterises the card SVG
at `qualityScale = max(4, dpr)`, so the 64×64 zone needs a ≥256×256 bitmap to
stay crisp; a 64×64 source would be stretched ~4× and appear pixelated.

**Produce every new sprite at 1024×1024**, named `<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`, in
`src/sprites/`. The legacy `<Name>_64_x_64.png` files are superseded
thumbnails and are not read by the generator.

## Progress (2026-09-29)

The mapping/resolver/tooling + pending-aware drift guard landed on `dev` as
commit `4b80741` (full unit suite green): `src/card-art-map.json` is now
`version: 3`. Real coverage rose from **65 → 95 of 171** unique cards.

**Duplicate names split (commit `874f419`).** On producer decision Q8 the two
duplicate card names were renamed, so all **173 card names are now unique**:

- business `Florist` → **`Flower Shop`** — keeps the existing rose sprite
  (renamed `Flower Shop_1024_x_1024.png`); its `upgradePath` and
  `Upgrade to Garden Center`'s `targetBusiness` both follow.
- event `Community Garden` → **`Garden Party`** — now needs its own art and maps
  to the `Investment__` category until then.
- staff `Florist` keeps its name; its business restriction is now
  `Flower Shop|Commerce|Culture`.

Card IDs are intentionally unchanged (`biz-florist`, `evt-community-garden`) to
preserve save/challenge compatibility. After the split, **95 of 173** cards
resolve and **78** still render `Fallback`: the staff `Florist` and event
`Garden Party` joined the pending set, giving **46 distinct source sprites** to
produce.

## Desired change (confirmed strategy)

1. **Upgrades (39) — duplicate target art under the new display name.**
   For each `Upgrade to …`, copy the art of its `targetBusiness` to a new
   source sprite named after the upgrade's `newDisplayName` (all 39 are
   distinct, no collisions, and none is already a sprite). Seven targets are
   themselves gaps, so their art must be produced first: `Cafe`,
   `Health Kiosk`, `Laundromat`, `Library`, `Park`, `Playground`,
   `Town Fountain`.
2. **Business / community-space gaps (9) — new art.** `Laundromat`, `Cafe` and
   all community spaces except `Community Garden`: `Park`, `Library`,
   `Playground`, `Town Fountain`, `Health Kiosk`, `Community Shelter`,
   `Public Art`.
3. **Staff (25) — new staff art.** **One sprite per staff role** (confirmed
   2026-09-29), produced by the producer. The split moved `Florist` (staff)
   off the shared business sprite, so all 25 roles need art.
4. **Events (37) — category mapping.** Map each event to a category sprite
   keyed by `(trigger, targetSynergy)`; **unique (bespoke) art per category**
   (confirmed 2026-09-29), produced by the producer. `Garden Party` joined the
   category-mapped set after the split.
5. **Resolver / map.** Extend the generated mapping (and/or `CARD_ART_ALIASES`)
   so both consumers agree and regeneration stays deterministic; keep
   `Fallback` only as the genuine last resort.
6. **Drift guard.** Add a unit test over `card-data.csv` asserting full
   coverage and failing when a new art-less card appears.

## Required art (derived)

| Group | Cards | Mechanism | New sprites |
|-------|------:|-----------|------------:|
| Upgrade | 39 | Duplicate `targetBusiness` art under each upgrade's `newDisplayName` | 0 new (39 copies) |
| Business + community-space gaps | 9 | New source art | 9 |
| Staff | 25 | New source art — one per role | 25 |
| Event | 37 | Unique `(trigger × targetSynergy)` category art — 12 categories | 12 |
| **Total distinct source sprites** | | | **46** |

Event categories for the 36 missing events (representative = an event with
dedicated art today in the same category, available to duplicate):

| `trigger` | `targetSynergy` | Cards | Existing representative |
|-----------|-----------------|------:|-------------------------|
| Incident  | (none)          | 9 | Tax Audit |
| Incident  | Culture         | 1 | Cultural Grant |
| Incident  | Entertainment   | 1 | Noise Complaint |
| Incident  | Food            | 6 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Health          | 1 | *(none — new)* |

# Intake Brief — Move level label to left (MS-0MUGRKEWZ0073327)

## Problem Statement
When a business or community-space card is upgraded it shows a gold level badge
("Lvl 1", "Lvl 2", …) in the **top-right** corner of the card face. This
position competes with the cost circle / right-hand text column and reads as a
secondary stat rather than the card's primary upgrade indicator. The badge
should move to the **top-left** of the card so the upgrade level is immediately
visible in a consistent, expected position.

## Users
- **Main Street player** — wants to identify an upgraded card's level at a
  glance when scanning the street grid and their hand.
- **Future example-game authors / designers** — reuse the shared
  `UpgradeOverlaySpec` contract and expect a single, predictable corner
  convention for the level badge.

### User Stories
- As a player, when I look at an upgraded card on the street or in my hand, I
  see the "Lvl N" badge at the top-left of the card, so the level is obvious at
  a glance.
- As a player, the badge position is identical whether the card is shown on the
  street grid or in the hand, so I never have to re-learn where to look.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] For every upgraded card (`level > 0`), the level badge is positioned at
      the card's **top-left**: in container-local coordinates (origin at the
      card centre) `levelBadge.x` is negative (left of centre) and the badge is
      **left-anchored** (`originX === 0`); the badge is no longer placed in the
      top-right (`x` must not be positive in the mirrored position). Verified by
      unit test on `buildUpgradeOverlaySpec` for level 1 and level 2 cards.
- [ ] The Phaser renderer (`applyUpgradeOverlays`) renders the badge with a
      left/top origin so the text starts at the top-left inset and remains fully
      inside the card bounds (no clipping past the left or top edge); the same
      overlay path is used by street and hand cards, so both move together.
      Verified by renderer/overlay tests.
- [ ] Badge content and styling are unchanged (`Lvl N`, gold `#ffdd44`, bold,
      10px) and no badge is produced for level 0 (base) cards.
- [ ] The dynamic SVG card-face generator (`generateBusinessCardSvg`) emits the
      level badge at the top-left (`x` at the card's left inset,
      `text-anchor="start"`) for consistency with the overlay, with its unit
      tests updated accordingly.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
      code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries
      (notably the module docs in `UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts` /
      `MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` and the level-badge references in
      `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md`).
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes, with all existing
      top-right level-badge expectations updated to the top-left contract.

## Constraints
- Card geometry is fixed: canonical **140 × 80** card with a **64 × 64 art zone
  at (8, 8)** (top-left) — see `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md`. The
  top-left corner is therefore occupied by the card art; the badge will render
  over the top-left of the art zone (mirroring the current badge overlaying the
  top-right). This is an accepted input to the brief (see Risks & Assumptions).
- Presentation-only change — no change to upgrade rules, card state, or level
  numbers.
- Reuse the existing overlay/badge primitives and gold styling; do not introduce
  new assets or a second badge component.
- Keep the overlay spec a pure data module (no Phaser imports) so it stays
  unit-testable in Node.

## Existing State
- `src/scenes/UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts` builds the badge at
  `x = Math.round(width / 2 - 4)`, `y = Math.round(4 - height / 2)` (top-right,
  4 px inset) with `color: '#ffdd44'`, `fontSize: '10px'`, `fontStyle: 'bold'`.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` (`applyUpgradeOverlays`) creates the
  Phaser Text and calls `lvlText.setOrigin(1, 0)` — right/top anchored — so the
  badge sits in the top-right.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` (`generateBusinessCardSvg`) emits
  `<text x="${width - 8}" y="13" … text-anchor="end">Lvl N</text>` (top-right)
  for upgraded cards. (This dynamic SVG path is exercised by unit tests; the
  runtime card face texture comes from the CSV-based template SVGs.)
- Tests asserting/pinning the badge: `tests/main-street/upgraded-card-rendering.test.ts`
  (positions the badge in the top-right), `tests/main-street/upgrade-overlay-spec.test.ts`
  and `tests/main-street/cash-line-overlay.test.ts` (badge presence/text),
  `tests/main-street/card-svg-generator.test.ts` (badge text).

## Desired Change
- Mirror the badge to the top-left: overlay `x = Math.round(-width / 2 + 4)`
  with `originX: 0` (and `setOrigin(0, 0)` in the renderer); `y` stays at the
  existing top inset so the badge remains on the top edge.
- Update the SVG generator badge to `x = 8` (or the chosen left inset) with
  `text-anchor="start"`.
- Update the module/JSDoc comments and the affected tests from "top-right" to
  "top-left". Exact inset values may be tuned during implementation as long as
  the badge is left-anchored in the top-left and stays inside the card bounds.

## Key Files
- `src/scenes/UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts` — level-badge spec `x` / `originX` and the
  "top-right corner" comment; primary change.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — `applyUpgradeOverlays` badge
  `setOrigin(1, 0)` → `(0, 0)`; comment.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` — dynamic SVG badge position /
  `text-anchor`; module doc mentions "level badge top-right".
- `tests/main-street/upgraded-card-rendering.test.ts` — update the top-right
  position assertion to top-left and assert left-anchoring.
- `tests/main-street/upgrade-overlay-spec.test.ts` — badge position/style
  expectations.
- `tests/main-street/cash-line-overlay.test.ts` — badge presence/absence
  alongside the cash line (position regression surface).
- `tests/main-street/card-svg-generator.test.ts` — SVG badge text/position.
- `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — level-badge placement references.

## Related Work
- **Potentially related docs:**
  - `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` — canonical 140×80 card and the
    `(8, 8)` 64×64 art zone that occupies the top-left.
  - `docs/main-street/ux-visual-audio.md` — upgrade level-up burst notes that
    reference the newly-rendered level badge.
  - `src/scenes/UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts` header — documents the overlay contract
    and the card-local coordinate system.
- **Potentially related work items:**
  - `MS-0MTV69NII000LW8I` — *Position end-turn coin matrix on left side of card,
    growing right* (bug, medium) — closest precedent: a card-face overlay
    repositioned from centre/right to left, landed with documented placement
    assumptions.
  - `MS-0MU9JYNZ3008AH5J` — *Update createCoinGrid defaults to left-anchored
    position* (task) — companion implementation task for the sister reposition.
  - `MS-0MUBVL4H80061B1E` — *Assign a dedicated 64×64 sprite to every Main
    Street card* (medium) — touches the top-left art zone that the badge will
    now overlay.
  - `MS-0MTRRYOT6001167R` — *Change the name of Physiotherapy business card to
    Physiotherapist* (task, low) — another card-face presentation tweak with
    test/doc churn.
  - Historical (core-repo) references cited in code: `CG-0MTORJ5FS006B0UN`
    (64×64 left-art layout) and `CG-0MP1VJVEK003I7VE` (display upgrade state on
    street-grid cards) — the layout and overlay these tests assert were
    introduced/refined there.
- **Automated report** (generated by `find-related`) — see the
  "Related work (automated report)" section retained below.

## Risks & Assumptions
- **Assumption:** "top left" means the card's top-left corner, mirroring the
  current right-side inset, with the badge left-aligned. Because the 64×64 art
  zone occupies `(8, 8)`–`(72, 72)`, the badge will overlay the top-left of the
  card art. That is accepted; if the producer finds it illegible over the art, a
  subtle backing chip or a slightly different inset is a small follow-up — it
  must be raised rather than assumed.
- **Visual-regression risk:** the badge colour (`#ffdd44` gold) may have low
  contrast against some card art; mitigate during implementation by checking the
  darkest/lightest card arts and, if needed, a 1 px dark outline (recorded as a
  follow-up if it expands scope).
- **Test churn:** `upgraded-card-rendering.test.ts` explicitly asserts a
  top-right position; update the assertions to the top-left contract in the same
  change rather than deleting them.
- **Scope creep:** do not restyle the badge, redesign the 64×64 layout, or
  change the cost circle / title / cash line. Record any broader card-face polish
  as separate work items.

## Open Questions
- None — the seed context (position the upgrade level badge at the top-left
  instead of the top-right) plus repo inspection of the overlay/spec/renderer
  provided sufficient signal for a clear brief. The only judgement call (badge
  overlays the top-left art zone) is recorded above as an assumption to be
  confirmed during review; no clarifying interview was required.

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers
- No interview conducted — the work-item description ("When a card is upgraded
  it gets a 'Lvl 1' label. Move this from the current location (top right) to
  the top left.") plus repo inspection of `UpgradeOverlaySpec.ts`,
  `MainStreetRendererStreet.ts`, and `MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` provided
  sufficient signal to draft a clear brief. No assumptions were left
  unrecorded; see Risks & Assumptions for the documented top-left-art-overlay
  assumption.

# Intake Brief: Serial Seller challenge (MS-0MUI7ZJK8003HY9J)

**Headline:** Add a run-local **Serial Seller** challenge that completes when the player sells 3 or more street businesses in a single game, with live progress in the challenge HUD and a persistent Steam achievement consistent with the existing 12 challenges.

## Problem statement

Main Street's challenge pool currently has no goal that rewards _selling_ businesses, so the sell mechanic (Manage Card → Sell) is rarely a deliberate strategic path. This item adds a new run-local challenge, **Serial Seller**, that completes when the player sells 3 or more businesses in a single game, and shows live progress toward the goal in the challenge HUD.

## Users

- **Main Street players** choosing a strategy each run.
- **Main Street players** who need to gauge progress at a glance.
- **The designer/producer**, who wants the new challenge consistent with the existing challenge/achievement system.

Example user stories:

- As a Main Street player, I want a challenge that rewards selling businesses, so that a sell-and-reinvest strategy is a viable route to bonus points.
- As a player, I want to see my progress toward the challenge (e.g. "2/3 sold"), so I know how close I am to completing it.
- As the producer, I want the new challenge mapped to a persistent Steam achievement like the other 12 challenges, so the achievement set stays complete and consistent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- New challenge template and category: `ch-serial-seller` (title **Serial Seller**, description "Sell 3 or more businesses in a single game.") is added to `CHALLENGE_TEMPLATES` with `category: 'economic'` and `rewardPoints === CHALLENGE_BONUS_POINTS`; a new `economic` member is added to the `ChallengeCategory` union; its evaluator returns `true` iff the cumulative count of sold street businesses in the run is `>= 3`, and `false` on an empty grid.
- System integration and progress UI: the template participates in deterministic `selectChallenges` selection; completing it fires exactly once through `evaluateChallengesAfterAction` (bonus points awarded, activity-log entry written, persistent-achievement bridge invoked); the challenge HUD tracker renders live progress (e.g. `2/3`) for progress-capable challenges while challenges without progress metadata render unchanged.
- Undo/redo consistency: undoing a street sale reverts both the progress count and any challenge completion it caused; redo re-applies them exactly once (no double completion, no stale progress).
- Achievement mapping and cross-repo dependency: `ch-serial-seller` maps to achievement id `serial-seller` in `CHALLENGE_TO_ACHIEVEMENT_ID`; the blocking dependency work item (`MS-0MUOLL8W2004A3D7`, discovered-from this item) supplies the `core` submodule `electron/achievement-manifest.json` entry and the Steamworks backend API name (`TCE_MAIN_STREET_SERIAL_SELLER`); the achievement completeness/drift tests pass once the dependency has landed.
- Testing and validation: unit tests cover the evaluator (empty grid, 1/2/3 sales), selection inclusion, progress metadata, HUD progress rendering, and undo/redo.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Only street/tableau sales via the **Manage Card → Sell** dialog count (the `sellBusiness` path, tracked by `state.soldSlots`). Hand sales (`sellFromHand`) and the legacy `sellFromTableau` path are out of scope.
- **No new game-state field.** Reuse `state.soldSlots` (it is cumulative for the interactive path, because sold cards stay on the grid and cannot be closed) so save/load and command snapshots keep working unchanged.
- Existing tests assert **12** templates and category coverage for the 5 existing categories; these must be updated to 13 and (optionally) to assert `economic`. The category-coverage assertion for the original 5 categories must still hold.
- The achievement mapping is enforced by `tests/main-street/main-street-achievements.test.ts` against the launcher manifest, which lives in the **`core` git submodule (a separate repository)** — the manifest entry and Steamworks API name are handled by a separate **blocking dependency** work item `MS-0MUOLL8W2004A3D7` (producer/external action), not run-local.
- The per-run selection count (`config.challengesPerRun`, default 3) and the end-of-game scoring formula are unchanged — only the template pool grows.
- The progress indicator must fit the existing challenge panel geometry (compact single-line rows); avoid layout regressions.
- All written output in UK English.

## Existing state

- `src/MainStreetChallenges.ts` defines the `ChallengeCategory` union (`synergy`, `placement`, `resource`, `upgrade`, `cross-cutting`), 12 `CHALLENGE_TEMPLATES`, `DEFAULT_CHALLENGES_PER_RUN = 3`, and `selectChallenges`/`evaluateChallenges` wrappers over the generic `@core-engine` challenge API. Evaluators are pure functions of `MainStreetState`. Selection is seeded from `config.challengesPerRun` in `src/MainStreetStateSetup.ts`.
- Challenge evaluation runs after every action (`evaluateChallengesAfterAction`) and at end of turn; completions are non-revocable during a run but are captured/restored by command snapshots (`captureSnapshot`/`restoreSnapshot` in `src/MainStreetCommands.ts`, which include `soldSlots`, `challengesCompleted`, and per-challenge completion flags).
- `state.soldSlots: boolean[]` marks sold street cards; sold cards remain on the grid as inert synergy anchors and cannot be closed, so the true-count is monotonic for the interactive path and is captured in undo snapshots.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts` (`refreshChallengeTracker`) renders the challenge panel as compact rows: indicator + title + description, with a `Challenges (n/N)` header. There is currently no per-challenge progress display.
- `src/MainStreetAchievements.ts` maps every challenge template 1:1 to a persistent Steam achievement; `tests/main-street/main-street-achievements.test.ts` guards completeness and drift against `core/electron/achievement-manifest.json`.

## Desired change

- Add an `economic` challenge category and the `ch-serial-seller` template with an evaluator counting sold street businesses and an optional progress provider.
- Add an optional `progress?: (state: MainStreetState) => { current: number; target: number }` field to the `Challenge` interface and render it in the challenge HUD tracker (e.g. `2/3`), leaving progress-less challenges visually unchanged.
- Add the `serial-seller` achievement mapping and create the blocking dependency work item for the `core` manifest entry + Steamworks API name.
- Update the affected tests (template count, evaluator/selection/progress/undo, achievement mapping) and documentation.

Design note: keeping progress as an **optional Main Street-specific** field on `Challenge` (rather than extending the generic `ChallengeDefinition<TState>` in `@core-engine`) keeps the change surgical and avoids touching the core engine. If a second progress-capable challenge is added later, promoting the field to the generic interface can be revisited.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetChallenges.ts` — add `economic` to `ChallengeCategory`, add optional `progress` to `Challenge`, add the `ch-serial-seller` template (evaluator + progress).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts` — render progress in `refreshChallengeTracker`.
- `src/MainStreetAchievements.ts` — add `'ch-serial-seller': 'serial-seller'` to `CHALLENGE_TO_ACHIEVEMENT_ID`.
- `tests/main-street/challenges.test.ts` — update template count (12 → 13); add evaluator, selection, and progress-metadata tests.
- `tests/main-street/main-street-achievements.test.ts` — mapping completeness/drift now includes `serial-seller` (green once the child manifest entry lands).
- `tests/main-street/` challenge-HUD/scene test — add progress-rendering coverage (extend an existing scene/HUD test or add a focused one).
- `core/electron/achievement-manifest.json` — **blocking dependency** `MS-0MUOLL8W2004A3D7` (core submodule): add the `serial-seller` entry with `TCE_MAIN_STREET_SERIAL_SELLER`.
- `docs/main-street/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` and/or `docs/main-street/prd-milestone-2.md` — document the new challenge/category if the challenge catalogue is described there.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetConstants.ts` — only if the progress indicator requires a layout constant tweak (avoid if possible).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Cross-repo achievement dependency (blocking, build impact).** The manifest lives in the `core` submodule and the drift guard (`tests/main-street/main-street-achievements.test.ts`) fails the build until the dependency (`MS-0MUOLL8W2004A3D7`) lands and the submodule pointer is bumped. Sequence the dependency first; this item must not reach `in_review` ahead of it.
- **Test friction from template count.** Several tests derive from `CHALLENGE_TEMPLATES.length`; only `challenges.test.ts` hardcodes 12. Keep the category-coverage list at the original 5 so `economic` is not required to have ≥2 templates (scope creep risk — do not add a second economic challenge here; capture as a separate linked work item).
- **Undo semantics.** Because completion is flagged on the `ActiveChallenge` and also recorded in `challengesCompleted`, redo must not double-add. Existing per-action reset (`completedChallengeIds.length = 0`) already guards this; add regression coverage.
